name: ঐরাবতেশ্বরর মন্দির, তিরুক্কোট্টারু
deity: ঐরাবতেশ্বরর রূপে শিব, ঐরাবত কর্তৃক পূজিত, দেবী বন্দার পূঙ্কুড়লি (সুগন্ধ কুণ্ডলাম্বিকৈ)-র সঙ্গে
period: তেবারম যুগ (৭ম শতাব্দীতে গীত); পরবর্তী চোল কাঠামোগত মন্দির
summary: তিরুক্কোট্টারু, কারৈকাল সীমানায় তিরুনল্লারুর কাছে, শিবকে ঐরাবতেশ্বরর রূপে — ইন্দ্রের শ্বেত হাতি ঐরাবত কর্তৃক পূজিত প্রভু — দেবী বন্দার পূঙ্কুড়লির সঙ্গে সম্মান করে। তিরুজ্ঞান সম্বন্দর কর্তৃক গীত একটি পাডল পেট্র স্থলম্, এর কিংবদন্তি দুর্বাসার মালা, ইন্দ্রের হাতি এবং সেই উপাসনার কথা স্মরণ করায় যার দ্বারা ঐরাবত এই বদ্বীপ মন্দিরে প্রভুর কৃপা ফিরে পেয়েছিল।

sections.history: Tirukkottaru, whose historical name is Tirukkottaaru, lies near Tirunallaru on the border of the Karaikal region, about 14 km from Karaikal and some 23 km from Mayiladuthurai. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Kaveri's southern bank, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar. Sources differ on the district — some place it in Tiruvarur district of Tamil Nadu, others under Karaikal — but it belongs to the Tamil Shaiva sacred geography of the lower delta. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: The temple is a Dravidian delta shrine with Airavateswarar in the sanctum and the goddess Vandar Poonkuzhali — also called Sugandha Kundalambikai, 'she of the fragrant tresses' — in her own shrine, with a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The lord's name Airavateswarar marks him as the Shiva worshipped by Airavata, the celestial white elephant.
sections.legends: The sthala legend begins with the sage Durvasa, who received a fragrant garland while worshipping Shiva at Kailasa and gave it to Indra, king of the gods. Indra set the garland upon his elephant Airavata. By the turns of that story — in which the garland is slighted and a curse follows — Airavata came to be parted from his lord's full grace, and here at Tirukkottaru the white elephant is said to have worshipped Shiva and regained it, giving the lord the name Airavateswarar. The temple thus keeps alive one of the elephant-worship legends dear to the delta's Shaiva tradition.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine. Pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail near Tirunallaru and Karaikal include Tirukkottaru among their stops.
sections.experience: Tirukkottaru offers the pilgrim a quiet shrine rich in the lore of Airavata, the elephant of the gods. Before Airavateswarar and Vandar Poonkuzhali, the visitor remembers the garland of Durvasa and the worship by which the white elephant regained grace — a small delta temple whose ancient name and legend outshine its modest size.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tirukkottaru is about 14 km from Karaikal, 5 km from Tirunallaru and some 12 km east of Peralam (on the Mayiladuthurai–Tiruvarur road); it is roughly 23 km from Mayiladuthurai. Karaikal and Mayiladuthurai are the nearest rail heads, with buses via Tirunallaru or Peralam and local taxis to the village.
